- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially >3 consecutive negative values), reduce forecasted price by 1–2% to account for bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is persistently above true outcome, consider mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the next 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (especially in first 10 days), adjust downward by 1–3% for next 10 days to reflect lagged reaction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (no sentiment), assume neutral market — model should not overreact; cap forecast deviation to ±1% of recent 7-day average.
